TWO DOMAINS ARE ABSENT AND NEITHER IS AN OVERSIGHT. cot_open_thoughts (0.776B) holds rows keyed {answer, chain, problem, src, tokens} with NO `content` field, so it contributes zero bytes to any sample and parity() divides by zero on it -- the first v2 gate attempt died there. never_used 0.0141 IS ABOVE the retired 0.01 threshold and that is not a failure: the threshold was demoted to reported-ungated in PR #69 for the reason tok.never_used_not_decidable records. The value is one draw inside a spread that is wider than the threshold.

WHAT THE SAMPLER FIX ITSELF MOVED, isolated by rerunning the EARLIER row's nine domains on the fixed tool -- same domains, same per_domain/shards, same vocabulary, so the only difference is the fix:

                    before      after
  hanzi whole-char  0.9890      0.9880
  ref fertility     1.4286      1.4286
  never used        (none)      0.0188
  bits/char         (none)      3.9266   <- first value on a full 800-row held-out set
  en fertility      1.3704      1.3365

So the three GATE readings barely move (hanzi -0.0010, ref fertility unchanged) and no verdict changes. THE FIX IS NOT WHAT MAKES bits/char CORRECT-VS-WRONG -- before the fix there was NO bits/char on that domain set at all, because it was never recorded. Searched the whole tree and all history: the only bits_per_char anywhere in facts/, docs/ or runs/ is this row's. Nothing published moves.

The v2 row's 0.9793 against the earlier 0.9890 is therefore NOT the sampler fix: the fixed tool on the old domains reads 0.9880. The 0.0087 gap is the two swapped domains (code_rp1t_dd09_full for code_py_rp1t, en_c4 for en_c4_stage2).

About the GATE's decidability, not about the vocabulary: whether 32,773 slots carry unreachable entries is a separate question this measurement cannot answer.

THE 0.01 THRESHOLD WAS A DELIBERATE CHOICE, NOT A PLACEHOLDER, AND THAT MAKES THIS WORSE. It enters at 143f5d4a (2026-08-29, 'tokenizer: gates green, and the two failures were both instrument or class errors'), whose message records the calibration: 'never used 0.0070 <=0.01 ok (regression guard: 234K params, 0.1% of the model)' over '106 tokens with zero occurrences in 142M'. So the guard was set 0.003 above a measured 0.0070 -- and 142M is essentially the scale at which the three-seed range measured here is 0.0110 (20000x24, 172M) and 0.0113 (shards axis, 167-187M). The threshold was placed INSIDE its own measurement noise on the day it was written, and one draw could not have shown that. The defect is not a missing calibration and not the wrong size: it is that a single draw at 142M does not determine the value to the precision the threshold needs.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, raised by 3b 2026-09-08 and recomputed here.

(1) THE 0.1% COST FIGURE IS PRICED AGAINST THE SAME SINGLE DRAW and inherits its uncertainty. 143f5d4a's '234K params, 0.1% of the model' is 229 slots x d_model 1024 = 234,496, and 229 is 0.0070 x 32,773 -- the same draw the threshold was set from. Across the readings in `data` the slot count runs 141 (0.0043) to 511 (0.0156), i.e. 144K to 524K params, a 3.63x band. The cost is real and small at every point in that band, so this does not change the decision to accept it; what it changes is that '0.1%' is one draw's value and not a measured constant.

(2) A GUARD WHOSE MARGIN IS INSIDE THE SEED SPREAD FIRES ON RESEEDING ALONE, which makes it a permanent-red candidate rather than a regression guard -- the failure mode 143f5d4a's own message says it was avoiding ('regression guards with the cost recorded, rather than targets that would be permanently red'). Of the nine readings in `data`, three exceed 0.01: one of the three seeds at 20000x24, and one of the three shard settings at seed 7 (0.0156, the same run, counted under both axes). Those nine are seven distinct settings, not nine independent draws, so treat this as 'it fires on reseeding at more than one setting', not as an estimated fire rate.
facts.audit: Three seeds at each of two fixed (per_domain, shards) settings, plus a shards sweep at fixed seed, on the v2 composition. Ranges 0.0042 (9000x16), 0.0110 (20000x24) and 0.0113 (shards axis) against a 0.01 threshold, so no measured setting separates pass from fail. STOPPED HERE by 4c 2026-09-08 rather than searching further settings: the metric is sound on nested prefixes, both axes move it by more than the threshold, and the deliverable became demoting never_used from regression guard to reported-ungated (e1-52) rather than finding a setting that happens to be quiet.
facts.refuted_by: a setting whose three-seed range is under 0.0033, which would make the gate decidable and give this fact a value; or a calibration of the 0.01 threshold on a corpus of this size, which would say what the gate should be testing in the first place

facts.uncertainty: The estimator's train-size dependence is measured, not assumed: at 3000 train rows the 16K->32K spread was +1.35%, at 30000 it is +0.43% -- the sign (bigger V slightly worse on bits/char) survives, the magnitude shrinks. The 20K->32K marginal is +0.33% at 30K. The repo's standing claim that bits/char is 'strictly monotone in size' (tokenizer_eval.py, the reason it cannot rank across sizes) does not hold on this composition at either train size. never_used is on 800 eval rows (~200K tokens) and is size-bound (tok.never_used_not_decidable); the load-bearing part is its direction -- larger V wastes more slots on the same text (6.1% at 16K to 23.9% at 32K).
facts.boundary: Intrinsic proxy; screens, does not rank (TokEval). The verdict on vocabulary size remains two pretrains differing only in vocabulary (unfreeze condition 3), not this sweep. This satisfies freeze condition 1 of the V=20,000 working target (4c, 2026-09-09): the 20K->32K segment is measured on the English proxy. Condition 2 (never_used re-measure on the first real synthetic textbooks) is still open -- the proxy is English WEB prose, not synthetic textbook prose, and 4c's standing instruction is that the real sample wins over the proxy. The embedding-param arithmetic at the pinned d's (scripts/p1_size.py, 4c 2026-09-09): shrinking 32,784->20,000 saves 13.1M tied params on p1-small (d=1024, 1.21% of 1.08B) and 26.2M on p1 (d=2048, 0.44% of 5.92B), and 39.0% of LM-head FLOP/token at both d's. The sweep conclusion itself is d-independent: bits/char does not depend on d, and the vocabulary is shared between p1-small and p1.
